candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Identify appropriate laboratory monitoring during therapeutic unfractionated heparin infusion.

options.A: Coagulation testing such as aPTT to guide dose adjustment, with platelet count and hematocrit monitoring.
options.B: Hemoglobin A1c and urine ketones as the primary tests for dose adjustment.
options.C: Thyroid-stimulating hormone and free T4 before every rate change.
options.D: A serum digoxin level and ECG as the primary heparin monitoring plan.

candidate.rationale: Full-dose unfractionated heparin therapy requires coagulation monitoring to guide dose adjustment. Product labeling also directs monitoring of platelet counts and hematocrit because bleeding and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia are important safety concerns.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Therapeutic unfractionated heparin dosing is guided by coagulation testing; platelet count and hematocrit should also be monitored.
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration / Laboratory Monitoring—coagulation testing for full-dose therapy; monitor platelet count and hematocrit
candidate.stem: An adult client is receiving a continuous IV unfractionated heparin infusion under an aPTT-based dosing protocol. Which monitoring should the nurse expect?
